If you've only been at it a month, you're doing great! Focus on your form and don't cheat yourself. You're going to see others in the gym doing all kinds of bizarre crap that allows them to lift heavier weights (swinging their hips while doing bicep curls, for example) - this usually puts unnecessary stress on joints/ligaments and is pointless. Unless you're training for a weightlifting competition, you are lifting to get strong. You get strong by not cheating on form, being consistent in your workouts, and staying healthy!

My final tip is - if you can afford it, get a personal trainer, even if it's only for a few sessions. Learn the proper way to lift weights. Make them teach you how to use free weights. Free weights are far superior. You are training all of your little stabilizer muscles that you'll need to lift anything in real life. Machines don't allow you to do that. You don't learn anything about balance or stability while you're strapped to a machine that's doing all of that for you. (Not all machines are terrible, but 99% of them are. There are some muscles, like rotator cuffs, that are hard to work without a cable pull.) Get a friend or hire the trainer again on occasion to make sure your form isn't slipping. Have fun!
